concerns.text: T008 defines a fallback to 'default 0.30' if research.md is missing. This silently relaxes FR-003 (≤30% constraint) by allowing a hardcoded default without the required 'Methodology for Parameter Limit' from T000. The spec mandates the limit be derived from research, not defaulted, to prevent arbitrary constraint relaxation.

T017a introduces a 'Time-Estimation and Subset-Reduction Fallback' reducing training samples to '[deferred]' if time > 2h. This violates FR-004 which mandates training on a 'defined OpenWebText subset ([deferred] samples)' where the definition is fixed in the research phase. Allowing runtime reduction based on time estimates weakens the experimental protocol defined in the spec.

T131 requires 'Capacity Normalization' analysis and a new field in trajectory.json. The spec (FR-009, SC-003) only mandates linear regression (slope, intercept, R²). This task introduces a new analytical requirement not present in the spec, violating the principle that tasks must not silently expand scope or alter the measurement protocol defined in the plan.

T128 implements a 'Thermodynamic Bounds' calculator and 'energy_per_accuracy_unit' metric. While SC-004 requires 'performance-per-FLOP' and 'performance-per-hour', the task introduces a specific 'energy cost' calculation (FLOPs * time) and a new metric name not explicitly defined in the spec's acceptance criteria, risking semantic drift in the reported results.

T126 implements a 'Rollback & Verification' state machine that increments the cycle counter on degradation. FR-015 mandates 'terminate early' if degradation ≥5%. T036 implements this termination. T126's logic to 'proceed to the next cycle' on degradation directly contradicts the mandatory termination requirement in FR-015, effectively weakening the safety constraint.
